rules.text: If the query image contains a large, distinct object (e.g., a person in a costume) that is explicitly present in the provided normal reference images, trust A (Agent) to correctly identify it as normal.

If the query image depicts a standard driving scene where the only difference from references is the time of day (e.g., daytime vs. nighttime references), trust A (Agent) to classify it as normal rather than flagging it as a contextual anomaly.

If the query image contains a small, low-contrast object on the road surface (e.g., a dark spot or shadow) that A flags as an anomaly but B classifies as normal, trust B (Direct) to avoid false positives on minor visual noise.

If the query image contains common urban elements such as pedestrians crossing, emergency vehicles, or bright digital billboards that A flags as anomalies, trust B (Direct) to correctly classify them as normal traffic conditions.

If the query image shows a standard highway or street scene with typical traffic flow and no obvious obstructions, trust B (Direct) to classify it as normal even if A identifies minor variations as anomalies.
The camera viewpoint is from inside a vehicle, with the dashboard or hood visible at the bottom of the frame.
The drivable road surface occupies the central and lower portion of the image, extending into the distance.
Ignore dark, elongated shadows or debris-like shapes on the road surface if they are consistent with low-light conditions or road texture.
Do not flag pedestrians standing on sidewalks or near curbs as road obstacles unless they are clearly stepping into the active driving lane.
Treat bright reflections, billboards, or light bars on vehicles as normal environmental features rather than defects or anomalies.
